transcript:
Header: 2026-07-16 15:00 PDT | Duration: ~56m | Recording: yes
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Erin Gomez (Redwood CSM), Maya Chen (Phoenix Head of ML), Liam O'Connor (CTO), Priya Kapoor (SRE), Diego Ramos (Product)

[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'll do a 30 second intro. Jordan from Redwood, AE. With me are Samir, our solutions engineer, and Erin who will be supporting the POC.
[00:07] Maya: Hi, Maya here. Thanks, excited — we want to scope this POC to understand cost and performance for our summarization use case.
[00:12] Liam: Yep, quick context — Phoenix runs an ingestion pipeline that turns long-form reports into concise summaries for customers. We currently use a hosted third-party API but costs are spiking. Main ask is: can Redwood demonstrate better unit economics without sacrificing latency and quality.
[00:28] Samir: Great, that's exactly what we'll focus on. Quick agenda: confirm workload shape, define success criteria, agree benchmark plan, and POC timeline.
[00:36] Priya: We're also sensitive to data residency and want VPC option eventually — but for POC hosted is fine if logs aren't persisted.
[00:42] Jordan: Noted. Maya, can you outline current throughput and token characteristics?
[00:47] Maya: Sure. Peak QPS is about 8 rps during business hours, average is ~2 rps. Typical input length ~1.2k tokens, outputs around 150-250 tokens. So round trip per request averages 1.4k tokens. Monthly active requests ~1.7M.
[01:05] Samir: Helpful. So for unit economics math we use tokens per request * requests to get total tokens. Do you have peak concurrency and acceptable latency SLOs?
[01:13] Maya: P95 target ~800ms for the summary endpoint, P50 around 200-300ms is fine. If P95 hits >1.5s it's a problem.
[01:22] Diego: Quality bar is also important — summaries must hit our ROUGE-like internal metric; we'll provide evaluation prompts.
[01:29] Samir: Good. For a baseline calculation, if avg 1.4k tokens per req and 1.7M requests/month that's ~2.38B tokens/month. At hosted API pricing we can model cost per 1M tokens. For example — rough Redwood hosted estimate at X quant/variant is $Y per 1M tokens — we'll put exact numbers in the spreadsheet.
[01:52] Liam: Can you walk through the knobs that move cost — batching, caching, quantization? We need to know where savings come from.
[01:58] Samir: Absolutely. Three main levers: 1) batching — increases throughput by processing multiple requests in one forward pass; effective for slightly higher latency tolerance. 2) KV/prefix caching — if requests share prefixes or repeated contexts we can cache KV cache to avoid re-computing. 3) model quantization / cheaper model variants — can drop per-token CPU/GPU cost, sometimes with small quality tradeoffs. Also routing policies — route non-critical traffic to lower-cost region or model variant.
[02:24] Maya: Our prompts vary but we do have a lot of similar intro text; caching might help. How much does batching reduce unit cost in practice?
[02:31] Samir: It depends on sequence length distribution and model. For long inputs like 1.4k tokens, batching gives decent GPU fill but the marginal cost per token drops maybe 15-40% depending on batch sizes and latency constraints. We'll simulate with your logs.
[02:46] Priya: For POC we can't expose production keys, so we'll provide anonymized logs. Also need to confirm SSO and KMS implications if we move to private later.
[02:55] Erin: We'll share our security deck and SOC2 docs after the call. For the POC hosted run, logs are ephemeral and we can scrub them.
[03:03] Liam: What's the recommended POC length?
[03:06] Jordan: Typically 4-6 weeks. Week 1: data handover and sizing; Week 2: small-scale benchmarking; Week 3: full run with different configs; Week 4: analysis and recommendation. If networking/VPC is required add 1-2 weeks.
[03:20] Maya: Sounds reasonable. Also need to validate quality — can Redwood run evaluations against our ROUGE suite?
[03:25] Samir: Yes. We'll run hem tests and return metrics: ROUGE, BLEU, and also human-sample checks. We'll include regression alerts if quality dips.
[03:34] Diego: Budget: we have about $30k for the POC phase — is that realistic?
[03:38] Jordan: Depends on the benchmark run scale. A focused 72-hour full load run to model production costs typically fits within that. If you want multi-config long-duration runs costs rise. We'll size the benchmark to fit the budget and show extrapolated monthly estimates.
[03:52] Priya: Regarding deployment: if we do dedicated later, what's the SLA and committed throughput?
[03:58] Samir: Dedicated gives predictable throughput and isolated capacity. We can size a pool to meet your P95 SLOs at target QPS. SLA depends on contract but we offer uptime and latency guarantees for Dedicated. We'll include rough config in the proposal.
[04:11] Maya: Can we see an example cost calc?
[04:14] Jordan: Yes I'll share a spreadsheet with two examples: hosted path (per-token pricing, with expected batching savings and cache hit assumptions) and dedicated path (monthly node cost + amortized per-token for storage/ops). Example calc will show best/likely/worst case.
[04:29] Liam: On caching assumptions what hit rate do you typically see?
[04:33] Samir: For summarization with reused intro prompts, maybe 5-15% KV cache hit initially; for templates or repeated contexts it can go higher. We'll estimate conservatively and run empirical measurement.
[04:44] Diego: Any hidden costs — egress, storage of KV caches, or evaluation compute?
[04:49] Erin: We'll call out egress and storage clearly. KV cache is in-memory per-instance but we can quantify memory footprint. Evaluation compute for the POC is included in the benchmark quote.
[04:58] Maya: For success criteria let's define a short list we all agree on.
[05:02] Liam: I'll add: 1) P95 <=800ms (or at least demonstrably achievable on Dedicated), 2) summary quality within 2% of current ROUGE baseline, 3) projected monthly cost reduction >=20% vs current vendor, 4) operational readiness (VPC/SSO if required).
[05:19] Jordan: Good set, we'll use those as the POC gates.
[05:23] Samir: For the benchmark plan we propose: ingest 7 days of representative logs, build a replay harness that mimics production concurrency pattern, run three configs — baseline hosted variant, hosted with batching & caching, and dedicated node with optimized kernels/quantization. Collect token counts, latency P50/P95/P99, throughput, and cost.
[05:44] Maya: How long will each config run?
[05:46] Samir: For stability we do 24–72 hours per config depending on budget. Even a 24-hour focused run at peak times will give good extrapolation.
[05:55] Diego: Will you simulate user-level state (KV cache warm-up)?
[05:58] Samir: We'll include warm-up runs to capture realistic cache behavior. We'll also test cold starts to understand tail latencies.
[06:06] Priya: For networking, if we need to test VPC connectivity what's the lead time?
[06:10] Jordan: Network setup for a POC VPC peering usually takes 5–10 business days depending on firewall rules. If it's required we should start that in parallel to logs handoff.
[06:21] Liam: Any legal/procurement gotchas for POC?
[06:24] Erin: We'll provide a POC MSA and an addendum for data handling. Low friction; typical customers sign an LOA and use trial terms. We'll share standard docs.
[06:33] Maya: On the subject of model variants, how do you approach selection? We care about hallucinations.
[06:38] Samir: We'll test a few open models and Redwood-verified variants. If hallucination is a risk we'll prefer more aligned / larger variants and tune prompts; the eval harness will flag regressions.
[06:47] Jordan: Quick note — competitors mentioned: customers sometimes consider Anthropic/Google offerings; we'll show Redwood's advantages around predictable unit cost and deployment flexibility.
[06:58] Maya: Wrap up: can you send the spreadsheet and a short POC plan by Monday?
[07:02] Jordan: Yes, that's Jordan's action item. Samir will send the benchmark plan. Erin will attach security docs.
[07:07] Liam: We'll aim to provide logs and ROUGE suite by end of next week.
[07:10] Jordan: Great. Thanks everybody. We'll follow up in email with the timeline and next steps.

Notes: occasional ASR noise — speaker labels may shift in places; some product names transcribed as "redwood-dedicate" or "KV cash" in the raw but clarified in the discussion. References: shared benchmark spreadsheet (link: https://redwood.app/sheets/phoenix-poc-benchmarks) and security deck (link: https://redwood.app/security/phx-poc).
